title: The dispatch resolves the tier's host, probes it, and refuses by tier
name: The dispatch resolves the tier's host,
description:
Today `dispatch` (packages/core/src/dispatch.ts:103-112) probes `config.dispatch.host` once, checks it is attendable, and passes the same string to `startRun` and `startAgent`. After this node the host is the one the node's tier resolves to from `dispatch.tiers` (read through `readConfigFromBase`, ADR 0019 — a run must not choose its own host), and `dispatch.host` is only what an unnamed tier gets, as the `unnamed-tier` decision says.

Concretely:
- one function in core takes the config and the node's tier and returns the host command line to launch (and the model, where the `tier-host-shape` decision makes it a separate field); every reader in dispatch.ts goes through it.
- `checkHost` runs against that host. A tier whose host is unknown (`UnknownHostError`), not installed, or not logged in throws a `HostError` that names the node, the tier, the host and the config key to fix — e.g. `high → opencode: not logged in; run \`opencode auth login\` or change dispatch.tiers.high`.
- the attended check at dispatch.ts:110 names the tier: `--watch` on a node whose tier runs Codex is refused with the tier in the sentence.
- `startRun` records the resolved host (and model) in the run record, so `Run.host` in packages/schema/src/run.ts is what actually ran.

Tests live with the code: dispatch tests against the fake hosts in test/integration/hosts (claude, codex, opencode) — one for a tier that resolves, one for the fallback, one for each refusal.

brief.approach:
Score 3, and smaller than the node's own text expects: `the-dispatch-picks-the-model-from-the-sc-c9n8` landed first (merged `0e3781be`) and already built most of what this node describes. Read `packages/core/src/dispatch.ts` and `packages/core/src/config.ts` before writing a line.

**Already true, verified in the tree:** `hostForTier` (`config.ts:198`) resolves a tier to a command line and reports `fallback` when the tier names none; `tierFor` maps a complexity to a tier; `dispatch` reads the node's brief, resolves the line through both, and uses that one line for `checkHost`, `adapterFor`, `startAgent` and `startRun`; `Run` carries `tier` and `fallback` (`packages/schema/src/run.ts`); the config is read with `readConfigFromBase` so a run cannot raise its own model (ADR 0019); and `test/integration/dispatch.test.ts:414-438` covers a tier that resolves, a tier that names no host falling back, and an unscored node. None of that is this node's to rebuild.

**What is left is the refusal, and only the refusal.** Today a bad tier host produces `${node} was not started (the high tier): opencode is installed but not logged in — run \`opencode auth login\``. It names the tier but never names the key a person edits, so the reader knows what broke and not where to fix it. The node's own text spells the target: `high → opencode: not logged in; run \`opencode auth login\` or change dispatch.tiers.high`.

Three refusal paths, all in `dispatch` in `packages/core/src/dispatch.ts`, all fixed by giving the `HostError` message the config key:

1. **`checkHost` says no** (not installed, not logged in, unreadable status). Append `or change dispatch.tiers.<tier>` when a tier resolved the line, and `or change dispatch.host` when none did — an unscored node's failure must not point at a tier key that had nothing to do with it. `checkHost`'s own `reason` already carries the host name and the sign-in command; do not duplicate either, wrap it.
2. **The tier names a host SOBER does not know.** `checkHost` calls `adapterFor(host)` on its first line (`host.ts:45`) and `adapterFor` throws `UnknownHostError` rather than returning — so a typo in `dispatch.tiers.high` escapes `dispatch` as a bare unknown-host error with no node, no tier and no key in it. Catch it around the `checkHost` call and rethrow as a `HostError` naming all three. This is the failure the second bound decision's cost line predicts — "a typo in a tier key sends the work to the default host" — except worse, because an unknown host does not fall back at all.
3. **Attended on a host that cannot be attended** (`options.attended === true && !adapterFor(line).attendable`). The sentence already names the tier; add the key, so `--watch` on a node whose `high` tier is Codex tells the reader which line to change.

Keep all three in the shape the file already uses: one `HostError`, one sentence, the node first. Write the key-naming as one small helper beside the existing `named` local rather than three string concatenations that will drift.

**Tests** in `test/integration/dispatch.test.ts`, beside the three tier cases already there and using the same `board({ tiers })` helper and the fake hosts under `test/integration/hosts/`. One per refusal: a tier pointing at a host that is not installed refuses with the node, the tier and `dispatch.tiers.<tier>` in the message; a tier pointing at a name no adapter knows refuses the same way rather than escaping as an unknown-host error; and an unscored node's refusal names `dispatch.host` and no tier key. Assert on the message text — the message *is* the feature here.

Nothing else changes: `hostForTier`, `tierFor`, the `Run` fields and every surface that renders them are already right and are not this node's to touch.

acceptance.proves: each refusal names the node, the tier and the config key to edit — including a tier pointing at a host no adapter knows, which escaped as a bare unknown-host error before — and the three tier-resolution cases c9n8 landed still pass
the config key a person edits is in the refusal itself, not left for them to infer from the tier's name
checkHost and the adapters are unchanged — the fix is in how dispatch reports their answer, not in what they answer
only the dispatch refusal paths and their tests changed: no schema move, no config change, no CLI, no dashboard, no MCP tool
no new name reached core's surface — the helper is local to dispatch.ts
